events.label: stopped_vehicle
events.note: Lime-green articulated bus (route 99) stopped diagonally across the middle of the intersection, rear section at frame x1200-1800 y700-1000. Verified by 0.5 s zoom sheets: the bus is pixel-identical at t=70,72,74,76,78 while cars, vans and a box truck flow past on its left. The signal governing this direction is GREEN from t=40 to ~t=76, so this is NOT a red-light queue and nothing is stopped behind it in that lane. Bus starts creeping again at ~t=80 and leaves the frame at ~t=86. Boundary uncertainty about +/-1 s.

events.label: jaywalking
events.note: Three young men (one in a white T-shirt, two in black) walk diagonally NE across the wide open intersection carriageway from the lower-left crossing towards the far kerb island at x1140-1290 y550-600. Confirmed on unmarked dark asphalt at frame (790-830,640-720), (1010-1060,650-740), (1120-1170,660-760) at t=90, and on plain asphalt at (600-650,750-840),(780-820,760-850),(960-1010,750-850) at t=86. Template-tracked trajectories: they appear to leave the marked zebra at ~t=82.3 (front man) and reach the far kerb/island at ~t=95. Cars and a bus pass within a few metres of them. Boundaries +/-1.5 s.

events.label: congestion
events.note: Intersection box and the approach lanes are packed nose-to-tail with buses, minibuses, vans and cars in every lane of the direction travelling right; the queue spans the full carriageway width from x=0 to x=1200, y=150-620. 1 s-step crops at t=216-220 show the signal is GREEN and the queue is CRAWLING, not stopped (a bus advances ~50 px/s, roughly 1 m/s), which distinguishes this from a plain red-light queue. Traffic starts packing at ~t=213 and the box is essentially clear again by ~t=243 (a red bus queue remains in the far carriageway at t=245-249). Boundaries +/-3 s; I could not verify the signal state continuously across the whole 30 s.

events.label: jaywalking
events.note: One to three pedestrians on the dark unmarked carriageway between the middle zebra crossing (stripes end at y~600) and the pink triangular island (kerb at y~780), in the band x600-1100, y620-950. A man in a white T-shirt with a red shoulder bag stands at (620-780, 620-740) for roughly 10 s; a man in a black T-shirt and beige trousers walks across (700,670) at t=185 to (1010,700) at t=188. WEAKER LABEL than the first one: some of these people appear to be loitering/standing rather than crossing, and I cannot prove they stepped off the kerb rather than the island. Boundaries +/-2 s.

notable_absence: accident: no contact between any road users and no vehicle against a fixed object anywhere in the 317 s. I looked for a stationary car in the middle of a lane, a cluster of vehicles at an angle, debris on the asphalt and a gathering crowd at all 7 overview sheets; the only crowd of pedestrians (t=128-145) is a normal group using the marked zebra crossing.
near_miss: no visible instance of sharp braking or swerving to avoid a conflict. Cannot be excluded - 2 s stills cannot resolve deceleration - but nothing in the stills suggests one.
road_obstacle: no debris, animal or fallen object on the carriageway at any time.
fire_smoke: no smoke or flame visible anywhere in the clip.

red_light: no vehicle crossed a stop line against a red. Every time I could read a signal (t=30, 82.5, 84.5, 86, 90, 94.5, 216-220, 245) the signal state was consistent with the traffic that was moving; the eastbound and westbound heads were red at t=30-35, 76-92, 245-249 and green at t=40-76 and t=216-220.
wrong_way: no vehicle travelled against its lane direction. All turning traffic used the same turning area in a consistent direction.
illegal_u_turn and illegal_turn: no U-turns and no turn from a clearly wrong lane observed in the clip.
solid_line_crossing and stop_line: no clearly observable solid-line crossing and no vehicle stopped past a stop line on red. Both need a resolution and viewing angle this camera does not give.

failure_to_yield: the two marked crossings were very heavily used (a group of ~15 people on the zebra at t=128-145, more groups at t=176-190) but in every case the turning traffic was stopped or slow before the crossing, so I saw no vehicle drive through a crossing occupied by a pedestrian.

The long stationary queue in the upper-left carriageway (frame x0-800, y240-520), present almost continuously from t=0 to t=317, is a RED-LIGHT queue, not congestion or stopped_vehicle: the signal for that direction is red whenever I checked (t=30, 82.5, 84.5, 86, 90, 94.5).

An orange food-delivery scooter with a red box stopped on the lower-left zebra crossing at t=30-41. Template tracking gives a genuinely stationary period of only about 6.0 s (x=604 at t=30.0 -> x=602 at t=35.5, then a slow creep away from t=36), which is under the 10 s rule, so it is NOT labelled stopped_vehicle.
The dense traffic at t=290-315 is NOT labelled congestion: 1 s-step crops at t=300-304 show vehicles moving at roughly 100 px/s (about 2.5 m/s), i.e. flowing rather than crawling.

The intersection bus jam at t=214-243 is not a bus-stop queue in my view (green signal, all lanes crawling), but I could not read the signal continuously, so a red-light explanation cannot be fully excluded.
caveats: All boundaries come from 2 s contact-sheet tiles refined with 0.25-1.0 s zoom sheets, so short events are good to about +/-1 s and the congestion start/end to about +/-3 s.

The clip is a fixed elevated wide shot; pedestrians are 40-70 px tall and the signal heads are only about 10 px across. I could separate red from green but never amber, and I could not see signal phase for a direction unless the head faced the camera.

Motion-dependent classes (near_miss, braking, illegal_turn, solid_line_crossing, stop_line, wrong_way) are close to unresolvable from stills at this scale. I treated all of them as 'not observed' rather than 'absent'.

The stopped bus may not be strictly zero-speed: its rear edge moved about 200 px between t=58 and t=67 (roughly 0.5 m/s, a crawl) before becoming pixel-identical at t=70-78. I set start=66.5 as the point where it becomes stationary, but a labeller using a looser speed threshold might start the segment anywhere in 56-67 s.

For the two jaywalking segments I inferred the entry/exit from where the pedestrians' feet are relative to the crossing stripes; foot position is only good to about +/-10 px (roughly +/-0.3 m) at this distance, which matters for the first step onto the road.

The second jaywalking segment (t=179-194) is the weakest label: the pedestrians there walk slowly or stand still, and I cannot rule out that some were on an unpaved shoulder rather than the carriageway. Drop it if a false positive is worse than a miss.
I did not systematically sweep the far carriageway (y<240) or the far right pavement (x>1500, y>450) at sub-second resolution; both are at the frame edge where resolution is worst.
